notes: Two standard searches covered Labcorp and Quest Q2'26. I opened neither the 10-Qs nor the full transcripts, so this rests on search-result summaries only. Labcorp groups women's health with oncology, neurology and autoimmune disease as 'specialty' testing. That group posted double-digit growth in H1'26, with no prenatal or NIPT split. Quest lists 'women's and reproductive health' among the clinical areas it is expanding. Neither source gave NIPT volume, price or mix. Neither gave any sequencing platform or sequencing cost statement. The Labcorp and Quest Q2'26 results did not report prenatal or NIPT metrics at all, so this source cannot test whether the NIPT market is growing or only reallocating. The headline lab volume figures (Labcorp organic accession volume +1.8%, Quest organic revenue +10.0%) are not NIPT-specific and not useful to the thesis.
how_to_mine: Only worth a deeper pass if the analyst wants to rule it out. Fetch the Labcorp 10-Q (EDGAR CIK 920148, filed around Jul 2026) and the Quest 10-Q (CIK 1022079). Grep each for 'prenatal', 'reproductive', 'women', 'Natera', 'BillionToOne', 'sequenc'. Then read the Q&A of the full Labcorp and Quest Q2'26 call transcripts for any women's health question. Expect little. Labcorp (Sequenom/Integrated Genetics) and Quest (Haystack, Natera-competing Qnatal) may mention NIPT only in an older 10-K risk-factor or business section.
